name: BEAM AGENT

intro.problem: Research in this group spans dozens of papers, textbooks and an evolving record of notes and code, and a general-purpose language model has none of that local context, so dense, accurate prompts have to be assembled by hand every time.
intro.value: A local agent over a tokenized library could turn a short request into a dense, cited prompt for a larger model [@lewis2020] and answer simple questions directly; folded into VELOCITY, a platform where only locked, versioned canon is trusted, every answer stays traceable to its source paper.
intro.approach: Papers and texts are converted with math-aware extraction [@blecher2023][@auer2024], chunked, and indexed by a pretrained embedding model [@xiao2023] beside keyword search [@robertson2009]. Nothing is trained on the documents, which keeps provenance intact. A local open-weights model retrieves, routes and composes the prompt, and a hosted model handles the hard reasoning.
intro.goals: Step 1 is deliberately small: a few papers and a few textbook chapters, tokenized and vetted with known-answer LLM tests and unit tests. Proving that tokenization returns the right passages is the major known bottleneck; the agent loop, cross-source synthesis and VELOCITY's canon layer follow only once it passes.

questions: Can a local index retrieve the right passage reliably enough to be trusted?
Does local context make the prompts sent to a larger model measurably better?
Can a locked, versioned canon keep agent output traceable without slowing the research down?

tagline: Local research agent over a tokenized library, inside the VELOCITY canon platform

caveat.text: Vetting comes first. Until known-answer tests show that tokenization returns the right passages, nothing downstream (agent loop, synthesis, canon platform) is built on it.

components.name: Step 1: tokenize and vet
components.subtitle: The known bottleneck
components.summary: A small corpus, tokenized and checked before anything is built on it. Initial ingest tests on sample papers are done; the vetting suite is the gate.

items.label: Corpus
items.detail: A few papers and a few textbook chapters, chosen so their correct answers are known

items.label: Ingest
items.detail: Math-aware conversion of equations and tables [@blecher2023][@wang2024], chunks tagged with paper, section and version

items.label: Index
items.detail: Pretrained embeddings [@xiao2023][@wang2022][@nussbaum2024] plus keyword search for jargon and symbols [@robertson2009]

items.label: LLM tests
items.detail: Known-answer questions: does the correct passage come back near the top, and are out-of-corpus questions refused

items.label: Unit tests
items.detail: Equations, tables and section boundaries survive extraction intact

components.name: BEAM PIPE
components.subtitle: The agent and the dense prompt
components.summary: The local model chooses its own tools (search the papers, search the record, open code, search again), loops until it can answer or says it cannot, and composes the dense prompt: restated question, definitions, equations and cited passages. It can propose actions but never commits them.

components.name: BEAM HALO
components.subtitle: Cross-source synthesis
components.summary: A batch job that clusters passages across papers and sweeps open problems against the textbooks to surface connections. This is passage-level proximity; any deeper insight comes from reasoning over what was retrieved, so it is only as good as the retrieval.

components.name: VELOCITY
components.subtitle: Four-layer canon platform
components.summary: Originally a separate idea, now the architecture BEAM runs inside. Agent output always lands in the dev layer; only a person promotes it to canon.

items.label: L0 Source
items.detail: Original papers, stored or linked, read-only

items.label: L1 Dev
items.detail: Researcher notes, code and AI prompts; mutable; a per-project switch decides whether AI is allowed

items.label: L2 Canon
items.detail: Frozen bundle bound to its paper; never edited in place, changes make a new version

items.label: L3 Site + AI
items.detail: Agent and read-only tool server over canon: summarize, rerun on new data, cross-reference; new work forks back to L1

items.label: Deployment
items.detail: Full-stack site, or a static front end plus a local server the researcher starts for read and write

components.name: Training, deferred
components.subtitle: Only if vetting shows misses
components.summary: Fine-tuning the embedding model or a reranker on question-passage pairs is cheap and keeps provenance, but waits until retrieval is measured to miss. Retrieval-aware fine-tuning and adapters stay on the shelf until then [@zhang2024][@hu2021].
